title: Infra steward pilot playbook: regulated workloads
content:
Purpose:
Quick, tactical playbook for sellers and solution engineers running pilots with infra/ops stewards at regulated enterprises. Focus: how to position Redwood’s private (VPC/on-prem) deployment as a risk-managed, operationally-friendly alternative to customer self-host or other vendors with loose control plane guarantees.

Intended audience:
- Solutions engineers running first 3 pilot engagements with regulated buyers
- Accounts team prepping for procurement + legal Q&A
- Field enablement and partner sellers

High-level framing (30s elevator):
- "Redwood Private is designed for teams that treat inference like a critical platform service, not an experimental component. We provide a private control plane (customer-managed networking + KMS integration) plus engineering tooling and SLAs so your infra team can operate predictably and pass audits without rebuilding model serving from scratch."

Core buyer concerns we must address (framing notes):
1) Data residency & auditability: show how logs, audit trails, and artifact provenance are retained in-customer and integrated with their SIEM/KMS.
2) Control-plane trust: explain clear separation between control signals (deployments, rollouts) and runtime data paths. Provide config examples for airgap / egress policies.
3) Upgrade and rollback mechanics: provide a simple rollback story; emphasize canary + automatic fallback policies to public/fallback models.
4) Security posture: KMS/HSM options, private networking, RBAC, and attestation hooks.
5) Operational burden: timeline and scope for SRE handoff, managed runbook options, and optional Redwood-run concierge for first 90 days.
6) Cost predictability: reserved capacity + burst rules vs. cloud spend surprises.

Buyer personas + tailored messages:
- CISO / Head of Security: emphasize audit evidence, attestation, KMS integration, and independent third-party pen test schedule. Ask: "Which compliance frameworks do you audit?"
- Platform/SRE lead: talk about autoscaling with shard-aware placement, KV cache persistence, and tracing hooks to integrate with existing observability. Bring performance numbers for 2–8k token workloads.
- Procurement / Legal: highlight contract constructs (data processing addendum, breach notification windows, SLA credits, liability cap boundaries) and an optional pilot SOW.
- ML/Feature owner: demonstrate stable latency, deterministic rollout semantics, and guidance for quantization/latency tradeoffs. Provide small benchmark scripts.

Competitive notes (quick scan):
- Competitor A (managed-llm-provider): sells a hosted-first story. Strengths: simplicity, shareable hosted demo. Weakness: limited on-prem package, fuzzy control plane separation, one-size-fits-all tenancy. Win angle: talk about separation of control and data plane and our stronger auditability.
- Competitor B (self-host appliance vendor): sells on-prem appliance + full ops. Strengths: self-contained hardware. Weakness: long procurement cycles, hard upgrades, opaque performance tuning. Win angle: faster pilot and incremental adoption (VPC first then airgap), hybrid rollback story.
- Competitor C (cloud infra vendor): strong network and identity integration but weak inference-specific optimizations and cost tooling. Win angle: show our batching/kv caching unit-economics and Redwood Optimize recommendations.

Objections + rebuttal scripts (concise):
- "We can just self-host and own everything."
  Rebuttal: "Totally reasonable — many teams start that way. The tradeoff is you take on the full lifecycle: kernel selection, hardware tuning, KV cache correctness, model rollouts and rollback testing, and SRE runbooks. Our private deployment removes the majority of that operational burden and gives you isolated control + observability you can hand to audit teams. We also offer a short, scoped handoff package so your team owns the platform at the end of pilot."
- "How do we know the control plane won't leak data?"
  Rebuttal: "Control signals are logically separated from runtime tensors in our architecture. We can show an architecture diagram and provide a readout of control-plane surface area, egress rules, and a sample attestation report from a previous enterprise pilot."
- "We need an airgap solution, is that supported?"
  Rebuttal: "Yes — we have a documented airgap deployment profile, plus an on-prem package with offline upgrade tooling. For pilots we often start with VPC+restricted egress and move to airgap as procurement clears."

Pilot design (recommended minimum):
- Duration: 6–8 weeks (short pilot recommended to get audit evidence and perf baselines)
- Scope: 1 production-ish route (customer dataset subset) + 1 eval set for quality regression checks + 1 SLO to validate (p95 latency, error budget)
- Success metrics: latency p95, tokens/sec cost, regression rate on eval prompts, ability to deliver audit packet (logs + attestation)
- Roles: Redwood SE (1 FTE fractional), Customer SRE champion, Legal/compliance reviewer
- Deliverables: deployment runbook, performance report, audit packet, 90-day handoff plan, optional 3-month managed run option

Pilot measurement matrix (example metrics to capture):
- Perf: p50/p95 latency, throughput at concurrency 4/8, model context warm-up time
- Cost: token cost per 1k tokens, GPU utilization and spare capacity for burst windows
- Reliability: error rate, failover success when canary fails, time-to-rollback
- Security: number of auditable events captured, KMS rotation tested, attestation checklist completeness

Collateral + enablement snippets (copy/paste friendly):
- Email subject line for intro to CISO: "Quick ask: audit evidence and pilot SOW for private inference"
- 2-line exec summary for deck: "Redwood Private lets regulated teams run LLM inference within their network perimeter while keeping first-class observability, rollback semantics, and KMS-backed key management — without rebuilding an inference platform from scratch."
- Demo checklist for SEs: deploy example stack in customer VPC, run model with 2k token test, capture logs to customer's SIEM, show rollback through console UI.

Unresolved questions / open work (TODOs):
- Create a short architecture diagram specifically showing separation of control vs data plane for legal/CISO reviews (owner: Marco)
- Template SOW for 6-week pilot that lists deliverables and acceptance criteria (owner: Aisha)
- Collect two sanitized attestation reports and a pen test summary we can share as NDA attachments (owner: Sofia)

Notes to self / field tips:
- Use language "steward" with platform/SRE folks — they respond to stewardship and SLAs more than "managed service" pitch.
- For procurement, lead with timelines and rollback SLAs — procurement cares about exit and risk transfer.
- Keep a short list of three must-have artifacts to satisfy auditors: audit packet, KMS rotation proof, and a rollback test report.

Appendix: sample audit packet components (quick list)
- Deployment manifest and version stamps
- Audit logs slice (first 72 hours + representative event types)
- KMS usage and rotation event log
- Rollback test snapshot and timeline
- Canary performance traces

End of doc — use this as an operational playbook for first pilots. Iterate after 3 pilots and fold field feedback into the public playbook page.
